book.title: From Smart to Lean: How to Design for Better Cities, Happier Citizens and Save the World

questions: How can a generative AI system for behaviour change be personalised, ethically robust and culturally sensitive at the same time?
What is the role of design in regenerating marginal rural areas, and how can AI tools amplify local agency without replacing it?
How do we measure the long-term effects of games on sustainable mobility habits, after the game ends?
How much of an intervention’s effect belongs to the intervention, and how much to the place: its streets, norms, climate and economy?
What can years of data from digital platforms for behaviour change tell us about questions they were never designed to answer?

areas.title: Games and behaviour change for sustainable mobility
areas.text: The core of my work, from trafficO2 in 2012 to MUV. People recognise the climate emergency and still take the car: games designed on solid theory — Self-Determination Theory, player typologies — can build motivation and habits that outlast the rewards.

refs.title: Involving people in the building up of smart and sustainable cities: How to influence commuters' behaviors through a mobile app game
refs.note: trafficO2, measured. The paper where a game on a student's phone stopped being an idea and became a change in how people travel to campus. No new bus line, no new cycle lane.

refs.title: Pursuing softer urban mobility behaviors through game-based apps
refs.note: Not a ban, a ladder. Each commuter starts from the habits they already have, and the game raises the target one step at a time.

refs.title: Engaging Gen Z in Transformational Games: How Complementary Features Enhance Core Mechanics for Sustainable Mobility
refs.note: 2,560 students, ten weeks, 6.86 tonnes of CO₂ avoided. The points did not keep them playing. Teams, content made by the players and a reason to come back did.

areas.title: Generative AI in design and sustainability
areas.text: How large language models can sit inside behaviour-change platforms, design studios and participatory governance, without hiding their biases or replacing the people they serve.

refs.title: GenAI for Sustainable Mobility Behavior Change: Building MUV's AI Driven Game Engine
refs.note: Written while we were still building it. A game engine that speaks to each player like a coach, and a federated architecture that keeps personal data where it belongs.

refs.title: AI, Metaverse and co-design for social innovation: an application protocol
refs.note: Tested in OSMOSI, between Milan and Palermo: AI reads the data and drafts the toolkits, a metaverse room lets people take part from afar. Neither replaces the facilitator in the room.

areas.frontier: Work in progress: digital clones for marginal rural areas — AI agents that amplify the expertise of local doctors, teachers, farmers and elders to support participatory governance where skills are scarce. Case study: the Madonie, Sicily.

areas.title: Design education
areas.text: What design schools teach, and what they leave out. A critique of a discipline still rooted in consumption, and proposals for an education that is transdisciplinary, ethical and driven by missions.

refs.title: Designing the Future: A Manifesto for Design Education
refs.note: The most polemical text I have signed. Design schools still train people to make us consume more. We propose an oath instead.

refs.title: Advancing Design Education: Integrating Service Design, Peer Mentoring and Generative AI in Project-Based Learning
refs.note: My studio, written up as a method: real briefs, students mentoring students, generative AI on the table. Teaching as research, not next to it.

refs.title: Design e transizione digitale: nuove sfide design-driven per l'innovazione tecno-sociale
refs.note: From experimental 3D printing to open-source AI built by hacktivists: cases where design takes technology back from turbo-capitalism and algorithmic control.

areas.title: Hybrid spaces, co-design and urban social innovation
areas.text: Places that are at once physical and digital — cultural hubs, living labs, neighbourhood spaces — and how their design supports participation. Action research with real actors, from Palermo to the Madonie.

refs.title: Designing Hybrid Spaces: Envisioning Plural Ecosystems and Socio-Cultural Practices
refs.note: Places that blur public and private, temporary and permanent, physical and digital — and the question that decides whether they work: who gets to run them.

refs.title: Urban Innovation Through Co-design Scenarios. Lessons from Palermo
refs.note: MUV was co-designed with citizens in Palermo's old town before a line of code was written. Co-design as a learning infrastructure, not as consultation.

areas.title: Sustainable cities: mobility, data and policy
areas.text: Urban mobility as the meeting point of service design, data, public policy and behaviour — and the wider question of how cities move towards circularity.

refs.title: Designing mobility in a city in transition: challenges from the case of Palermo
refs.venue: TeMA Journal of Land Use, Mobility and Environment
refs.note: Palermo in 2014, changing its mobility faster than its habits. The first time the distance between new infrastructure and old behaviour became my research question.

refs.title: Measuring the Change Towards More Sustainable Mobility: MUV Impact Evaluation Approach
refs.note: How do you prove that a game changed a city? The evaluation framework we built for MUV before the results came in, so the results could not choose it.

refs.title: A Win-Win Scheme for Improving the Environmental Sustainability of University Commuters' Mobility and Getting Environmental Credits
refs.note: 357 students and one app, trafficO2. The proposal: turn the energy they save on the way to campus into white certificates the university can trade, and give the value back as lower fees.

refs.title: Circular Cities: A Systematic Literature Review of Urban Strategies for Sustainable Transitions
refs.note: A review led by colleagues in energy engineering, with a conclusion my own work keeps meeting: circular cities move only where digital tools, participation and local policy move together.

areas.title: Cooperatives, housing and community
areas.text: How service design and digital tools can support mutual values and cohesion in housing cooperatives.

refs.title: Habitat e servizi. Ripensare l'abitare cooperativo
refs.venue: in Come fare casa. Abitare cooperativo e architettura dei luoghi domestici, Quodlibet
refs.note: Written for Confcooperative Habitat's seventieth anniversary: housing cooperatives as service systems, and what living together needs beyond the walls.

refs.title: New digital instruments for the community building in housing cooperatives
refs.note: Digital tools for cooperatives that do not replace the members' meeting. They make it easier to hold.
